3679.note: Climate system 2 and higher cannot exceed climate system 1's value.

3687.note: The outdoor temperature at which the curve correction is applied. The correction affects a ±5 °C range around this point.

3688.label: Change in curve
3688.note: Correction applied to the calculated supply temperature at the set outdoor temperature point. Positive means a higher supply temperature (more heat).

1942.note: Live status of the temporary hot water increase.

1233.label: Temp. lux forces start of hot water demand (read-only)

1777.note: The underlying hot water demand mode with Smart Price Adaption and Smart control influence excluded.

2685.note: Read-only — shows the date of the next scheduled Legionella sanitisation cycle.

1829.note: Live status of the circulation pump GP11. There is no separate on/off setting to enable circulation directly — activation happens only via the AUX output assignment in menu 7.4, per the warning above.

12396.label: Active days (period 1)
12396.range: 0 – 127 (bitmask: Mon=1 Tue=2 Wed=4 Thu=8 Fri=16 Sat=32 Sun=64)
12396.note: 127 = all days, 31 = weekdays only (Mon–Fri), 96 = weekend only (Sat+Sun)

12403.label: Stop time (period 1)
12403.note: Stop time for circulation period 1 in seconds from midnight.

12397.label: Active days (period 2)
12397.note: Active days bitmask for period 2. 1=Mon, 2=Tue, 4=Wed, 8=Thu, 16=Fri, 32=Sat, 64=Sun. Add values for multiple days. 127 = all days.

12398.label: Active days (period 3)
12398.note: Active days bitmask for period 3. 1=Mon, 2=Tue, 4=Wed, 8=Thu, 16=Fri, 32=Sat, 64=Sun. Add values for multiple days. 127 = all days.

12399.label: Active days (period 4)
12399.note: Active days bitmask for period 4. 1=Mon, 2=Tue, 4=Wed, 8=Thu, 16=Fri, 32=Sat, 64=Sun. Add values for multiple days. 127 = all days.

12400.label: Active days (period 5)
12400.note: Active days bitmask for period 5. 1=Mon, 2=Tue, 4=Wed, 8=Thu, 16=Fri, 32=Sat, 64=Sun. Add values for multiple days. 127 = all days.

56150.label: Operating prioritisation
56150.note: Shows what the system is currently working on: Heating, Hot water, Cooling, or Pool. Controlled by the operating prioritisation algorithm (menu 7.1.10.1). In auto mode the firmware balances demands automatically; in manual mode you set the minimum time for each function.

2022.label: Current status
2022.note: Shows the system's current operating mode as a decoded bitfield. Multiple modes can be active simultaneously — for example Heating and Hot water can run concurrently when a tank immersion heater is present.

781.label: Degree minutes (heating)
781.note: Degree minutes (DM) measure accumulated heating demand. The value becomes more negative as the house cools below setpoint. The compressor starts when DM reaches the threshold set in menu 7.1.10.3 (default −60 DM). Returns toward 0 as heating is delivered. A slow drift toward more negative values on a mild day can indicate the heating curve slope (menu 1.30.1) is set too low; a rapid swing suggests high heat loss or…

1708.label: Calculated supply temp climate system 1
1708.note: The firmware's calculated target supply temperature for climate system 1, derived from the heating curve and current outdoor temperature. This is the temperature the system is aiming to deliver, not necessarily what BT25 currently reads.

57.label: External supply line (BT25)
57.note: Actual supply line temperature measured at BT25 — the water leaving the heat pump toward the climate system. Compare with the calculated supply temp (1708) to see how closely the system is tracking its target.

121.label: Return temperature (BT71)
121.note: Return line temperature measured at BT71 — the water coming back from the climate system. The difference between supply (BT25) and return (BT71) indicates how much heat the system is delivering to the building.

2691.label: Cooling degree minutes
2691.note: Cooling degree minutes measure accumulated cooling demand. Becomes more positive as the house warms above the cooling setpoint. Active cooling starts when this reaches the threshold set in menu 7.1.10.3.

2695.label: Calculated cooling supply climate system 1
2695.note: Firmware-calculated target supply temperature for cooling in climate system 1.

734.label: Supply temperature cooling (BT64)
734.note: Actual supply temperature measured at BT64, used during active cooling operation.

2855.label: Controlling hot water sensor (BT6)
2855.note: Temperature measured by BT6, the mid-tank sensor that controls when the heat pump considers hot water production complete. The pump stops charging when BT6 reaches the configured stop temperature.

54.label: Average outdoor temperature (BT1)
54.note: Filtered average of BT1 over the period set in menu 7.1.10.2 (default 24h). The heating curve uses this averaged value rather than the instantaneous outdoor temperature, smoothing out short-term weather fluctuations.

2792.label: Charge pump speed (EB101-GP12)
2792.note: Current speed of the charge pump GP12 (inside the EB101 outdoor unit) as a percentage of maximum. In auto mode the firmware regulates this to maintain the correct flow through the heat pump.

1838.label: External heating medium pump (GP10) status
1838.note: Status of GP10, the external heating medium pump in the hydraulic circuit between the SMO S40 and the climate system. ON means GP10 is running.

1716.label: Cooling status
1716.note: Confirms whether the system is currently in active cooling mode. ON means the compressor is running in cooling direction with the reversing valve shifted.

3170.label: Requested compressor frequency (EB101)
3170.note: The frequency the control system is requesting from the compressor. If the actual frequency (3096) is significantly lower than requested, protection mode may be active — check point 3097.

2688.label: Blocked compressors
2688.note: Number of compressors currently blocked from starting. A non-zero value means the firmware is preventing one or more compressors from running due to an alarm condition or blocking input.

55749.label: Block new compressor
55749.note: Whether starting an additional compressor (in a multi-compressor installation) is currently blocked.

2495.label: Discharge (EB101-BT14)

2497.note: Temperature of the refrigerant gas entering the compressor on the low-pressure side. Used together with the evaporator temperature to calculate superheat.

993.note: High-pressure side refrigerant pressure expressed as a saturation (dew-point) temperature — not an actual temperature measurement. 2767.note: Evaporator coil temperature (BT16). The defrost function monitors this sensor — if it falls below the configured start temperature, the defrost index begins counting.

3095.label: Low pressure (EB101-BP8)

840.note: Minutes remaining until the next defrost cycle. Counts down to 0, at which point active or passive defrosting starts depending on outdoor temperature.
